correctness.rationale: Direct integration gives H_g z^k= sum_j n_j b_j/(n_j+k) z^{n_j−1}. Factor through V with columns v_j(k)=sqrt(n_j)/(n_j+k) and U=V*. Under x=e^t, normalized continuous kernels become separated translates of h(t)=1/(2cosh(t/2)). Their Gram kernel K(s)=|s|/[2sinh(|s|/2)] has summable off-diagonals, yielding an upper Riesz bound; a triangular Fourier minorant for separated log n_j and nonzero h-transform gives a strictly positive lower bound. Integer step sampling has derivative Hilbert–Schmidt error with decaying tail since sum n_j^-2 finite. Tail lower bound plus injectivity from vanishing Hausdorff moments of analytic F(t)=sum c_j sqrt(n_j)t^{n_j−1} yields global bounded-below V. Thus V* surjective with bounded right inverse, and approximation-number ideal inequalities show a_k(H_g) comparable with a_k(D), uniform in k,p,coefficients. Includes boundedness, compactness, S_p and realizable decay consequences, without assuming finite tests prove infinite Riesz bound.
